content:
Carlos has Mesa Vista 4C down as wrapped from its June turn and wants it released for listing. Brooke is ready to put it on the market on his word. I am not signing off on it until I have run my own pass, so before anyone lists it I need the real state of that turn.

The unit moved out in the middle of June with a target-ready date at the end of the month, which has already come and gone. The two scopes that carried this turn were the deep clean and the interior repaint. I need to know whether both are genuinely closed and signed off or still open, and I want the vendor side reconciled too. A scope that is billed but not finished, or finished with the bill still sitting unpaid, does not count as closed to me. There is also a re-inspection on the calendar for the middle of this month, and it factors into whether I can call this one done.

When you have the actual picture, record your QC determination on that turn and give me the call: if it is genuinely marketing-ready, sign it off; if it is not, say so plainly and hold it, because it does not go to listing until every outstanding scope is closed and signed off. Open a ticket on the issue tracker spelling out exactly what is still left on it, post where it lands in the make-ready channel, and get an email together for Carlos with the specifics. If I am holding it back, Brooke needs to hear it from us before she markets it.
I will check local report files, Airtable
records, Slack discussions, QuickBooks bills, Linear issues, and Google Calendar events related to Mesa Vista 4C to determine the exact
status of the turn.

- Obtain final written QC sign-off from Jaime Salinas before Brooke Phillips releases the unit to the market.

parameters.body:
Hi Carlos,

I am writing to inform you that following my Quality Control pass today (July 1, 2026), I am holding sign-off on Mesa Vista 4C and cannot release it for market listing at this time.

The unit's target-ready date was June 30, 2026. Per Star PM Quality Control policy, a turn is only considered done and market-ready when every outstanding scope is genuinely completed, inspected, and reconciled on the vendor side. Scopes that have been finished or billed but still sit unpaid in QuickBooks do NOT count as closed.

Here is the exact state of the open scopes and blockers on Mesa Vista 4C:

1. Deep Clean Scope (Sunshine Cleaning):
   - Vendor bill #2026-SC-4C ($387.00) sits UNPAID in QuickBooks (Balance: $387.00).

2. Interior Repaint Scope (Pete Donovan / Permian Make-Ready):
   - Main repaint bill #PD-2026-09 ($1,340.00) sits UNPAID in QuickBooks (Balance: $1,340.00).
   - Closet trim touch-up bill #2026-519 ($85.00) sits UNPAID in QuickBooks (Balance: $85.00).

3. Scheduled Re-Inspection:
   - The QC re-inspection scheduled on the calendar for the middle of July 2026 must be conducted and passed before final QC clearance.

Next Steps to Release for Listing:
- Process and settle all outstanding QuickBooks vendor bills for Sunshine Cleaning and Pete Donovan.
- Complete and pass the mid-July QC re-inspection.
- Obtain final written QC sign-off from Quality Control prior to marketing.

I have updated the Airtable Make-Ready turn record (Notes updated, Status remaining In Progress), opened Linear issue OPS-1000 (https://linear.app/synthetic/issue/OPS-1000) to track these items, and posted this determination in #make-ready.

Brooke (CC'd) — Please hold off on listing Mesa Vista 4C on the market until all open vendor bills are paid and the mid-July QC re-inspection is completed and signed off.

Best regards,
